### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f1340f32fa7594793d379cf024f5b0dd39f7b013`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md + packages/spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts, packages/spec/src/security/index.ts, packages/spec/package.json, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/app-default-permission-set.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, content/docs/references/marketplace/marketplace.mdx, .changeset/25773-published-package-default-permission-set.md, packages/skills/package.json

Face: governed rule text (`skills/**`) + published spec file (`packages/spec/src/**/*.zod.ts` ships in `files[]`). Inputs: card #25773 body and comments 6397310741 / 6407727166 / 6408339288, ruling record 6341690661 on #25083, PR #25930 body, file list, net diff `cb0a2fcf..f1340f32` (merge-base `cb0a2fcf`), check-runs on `f1340f32`. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (fleet account; no external-author note owed).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The only `packages/spec/src/**` hunk is inside the `/** # Marketplace Protocol … */` module doc block of `marketplace.zod.ts` (L31–L40: one new `## What a published package declares` paragraph, one trailing-space fix). No schema, key, enum value, export or `.describe()` moved; `CONSUMER_INSTALLABLE_TYPES` import and every `*Schema` below are byte-identical. No new spec key, so the land-with-first-reader rule is not engaged. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct for this diff.
2. **Fidelity to consequence (ii) — right, no scope creep.** The ruling orders text only: 「every published package declares one anchor-safe `isDefault: true` set」 in `security.md` (semantics → requirement) and the marketplace docs. The diff is four files, all prose/doc-block/changeset; no lint rule, runtime branch, schema or gate was added. The `security.md` bullet states the rule as a predicate an author can run, naming the symbol rather than paraphrasing it, as the card asked.
3. **The predicate exists and means what the text says — right, with one precision note.** `describeAnchorForbiddenBits(def, anchor: 'everyone' | 'guest', context?)` is defined in `packages/spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts` L192–L215, re-exported by `export * from './high-privilege'` (`security/index.ts` L21), and `@objectstack/spec/security` is a real subpath in `packages/spec/package.json#exports`. For `'everyone'` it returns `describeHighPrivilegeBits(def, context)` and otherwise `null` (L203–L205), i.e. `null` ⇔ no platform/undeclared `systemPermissions`, no VAMA, no delete/transfer/export bit — exactly the anchor-safe reading the text gives. Precision note for the approver: the text shows the two-argument call; the gates pass the stack's declared capabilities as the third argument (`anchorContext` in lint L966, `capabilities` in the derivation L660), and without it an app capability in `systemPermissions` reads as forbidden (`high-privilege.test.ts` L162 vs L163). The call as written is therefore stricter than the gate, never looser — a set it passes is anchor-safe — and the bullet's next sentence (`systemPermissions` may name only app capabilities declared under `capabilities:`) carries the context semantics. Acceptable at this token budget; noted, not a defect.
4. **The named refusals exist — right.** Lint: `SECURITY_ANCHOR_HIGH_PRIVILEGE = 'security-anchor-high-privilege'` (`validate-security-posture.ts` L129), applied with `severity: 'error'` to every `ps.isDefault === true` set via `describeAnchorForbiddenBits(ps, 'everyone', anchorContext)` (L966–L983). Binding: `suggested-audience-bindings.ts` imports the predicate (L81) and the `everyone` derivation withholds an offending set with reason (L660–L661, `EVERYONE_POSITION = 'everyone'` from `spec/identity/position.zod.ts`); `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion` (L995) runs the same gate. Boot: `everyoneBaseline` in `security-plugin.ts` L2237–L2243 still refuses via `describeHighPrivilegeBits`. The old wording 「lint and boot refuse …」 became 「lint … and the binding refuse it」; the boot-time withhold is the binding derivation re-run, so the meaning survives.
5. **The honesty clauses are true — right.** 「With none, invited members get nothing until an admin assigns each; no gate counts them」 / mdx 「no gate refuses a package that declares none, or more than one」: `appDefaultPermissionSetName` (`app-default-permission-set.ts`) returns the first `isDefault` set's name or `undefined`, with no diagnostic; the only `isDefault` counting in `packages/lint` is flow out-edges (`lint-flow-patterns.ts` L1187), not permission sets. Nothing in the cited code refuses zero or many. The published text states the gap instead of implying enforcement.
6. **Token ratchet paid in-file — right.** Recomputed with the gate's own convention (`ceil(utf8 bytes / 4)`, `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` header) from the blobs, no local run: `cb0a2fcf` 10250 B → 2563; `f1340f32` 10244 B → 2561; pinned ceiling `['skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md', 2563]` (L555) untouched (script not in the diff). Lines 220 → 220, so no re-wrap is counted as savings. Deletions and where their meaning lives: (a) `stack.zod.ts` path aside — the schema name `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` stays; (b) `rls.zod.ts` parenthetical — the source line stays, the table above it already lists the grammar; (c) `field.zod.ts` parenthetical — the section heading already names `secret` + `requiredPermissions`; (d) ADR-0105 §「Today's two postures」 pointer — the paragraph itself still states both postures and keeps ADR-0093, ADR-0132 and the tenancy-modes URL (the §-level pointer to `docs/adr/0105` L68 is the one real loss, minor); (e) 「plugin-security's FieldMasker enforces it. The real channels are:」 → 「(FieldMasker). Two more channels:」 — exactly two channels follow (`secret`, `requiredPermissions`); (f) the capability clause folded into the anchor-safe sentence, which is what the predicate refuses in `systemPermissions`. No meaning the file carried is gone.
7. **Marketplace page regenerated, not hand-edited — right.** `marketplace.mdx` keeps its `AUTO-GENERATED — DO NOT EDIT` banner; the generator demotes module-doc headings one level (`#` → `##`, `##` → `###`, matching the neighbouring `### Platform Management Flow`), and the nine added mdx lines are the nine source lines verbatim. The CI sync step (`Check generated reference docs are in sync with the spec`, lint.yml L5469, job `Type Check · source gates`) is `continue-on-error: true`, so that job's colour is not the evidence here; the textual comparison above is.
8. **Card closure — right.** `Fixes #25773` is correct: all three 「What to change」 items (skill text, marketplace source + regenerated page, ratchet paid in-file) land in this PR; the card's two boundary items (gate enforcement, hotcrm#2231) are explicitly not this card.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/skills` (`private` unset, `files: [dist, …]`, `dist` is `skills/**` copied by `scripts/sync-catalog.mjs`) ships the edited `rules/security.md` → published text, **`patch`**.
- `@objectstack/spec` (`files[]` includes `src/**/*.zod.ts`) ships the edited doc block → published text, **`patch`**.
- Changeset `.changeset/25773-published-package-default-permission-set.md` names exactly these two packages at `patch`, carries line-initial `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` matching the PR body, and its prose matches the diff (requirement, predicate, refusals, honesty clause, in-file trims). Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, `none` takes `patch` and a diff that publishes from a released package is never `skip-changeset`. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` — nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings` 「carrier: maintainer — no gate refuses a package that declares none or more than one」: **ESCALATE (maintainer-only, non-blocking).** The ruling orders the text; the card's boundary says a publish-time gate needs the maintainer's own word; the published text already states the absence honestly (①5). Nothing for this PR to do; the question rides to the maintainer with the Tier H approval reading of this PR body (「Acceptance notes」).
- `deviations`: attribution link points at the card thread (harness block) and the worktree was kept — neither touches the diff; no action.
- Dev-reported local gate runs (113 families, `check:generated`, spec build/typecheck) are the dev's evidence; this record's gate reading is the head's check-runs below.
- Observation for the lane seat, not a diff fact: the PR is `draft: false` while the claim (6407727166) said Tier H 「stays draft after an at-tier contract review PASS」. Readiness changes nothing here — the governed queue guard still requires a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval — but the seat may want to reconcile the claim's wording with the relay's `pr_create` shape.

No `failure` on the head; the second landing condition (all checks green) holds at this reading. Tier H: this PASS is the first landing condition; the PR still waits for a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval.
